History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
35-year-old man with 3–3.5 month history of loss of appetite, low energy, low mood, episodic palpitations/shortness of breath in lifts, headaches and nausea, and ~1 stone weight loss over 6 months; past history of hypothyroidism off thyroxine. Blood tests arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Reduced appetite and energy.  
• Timeline:  
  – Appetite ↓ and fatigue began ≈ 3–3.5 months ago (after changing to new law firm).  
  – Weight loss (~1 stone) gradual over ≈ 6 months.  
  – Palpitations/SOB episodes mainly when using elevator; duration not specified.  
• Associated symptoms: Low mood, headaches, episodic nausea, decreased libido (“nightly activities” concerns from wife).  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: SOB/heart racing occurs in lift; no clear food triggers for nausea.  
• Pertinent negatives: No chest pain, no cough, no diarrhoea, no blood or mucus in stool, bowels normal, no vomiting, no acid reflux.  
• Patient reports limited recent physical activity, so exertional tolerance uncertain.

Past Medical History:
• Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid) – previously treated with thyroxine; patient stopped medication after changing doctor; last thyroid blood test “long time ago.”

Medications:
• Thyroxine – dose/route/frequency not documented; currently stopped.  
Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
• Occupation: Lawyer; changed firm 3–3.5 months ago.  
• Marital status: Married.  
• Exercise: Not walking much recently due to low energy.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs: Not discussed.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• No physical examination performed; no vitals documented.

Investigations:
• Planned: Comprehensive blood panel (FBC for anaemia, renal profile, liver function, thyroid function tests, vitamin levels). No results yet.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Fatigue, weight loss, low mood:
  • DDx: Hypothyroidism relapse, anaemia, nutritional deficiency, depression, other systemic illness.  
  • Plan: Order bloods as above; review results; arrange follow-up. Consider physical exam and further work-up depending on findings.

Issue 2 – Episodic palpitations and shortness of breath:
  • Possible anxiety-related, arrhythmia, endocrine cause.  
  • Plan: Educate patient on red-flag symptoms (persistent chest pain, worsening SOB) → A&E. Reassess after labs; consider ECG and cardiac evaluation if episodes persist.

Issue 3 – Hypothyroidism, medication non-adherence:
  • Plan: Check TFTs; restart or adjust thyroxine once results available; counsel on importance of adherence.

General Plan Items:
• Patient to phone support number in app to schedule blood test.  
• Results will trigger text to book review; patient advised to seek care sooner if deterioration occurs.  
• Safety-netting reiterated regarding chest pain, vomiting, or bowel habit changes.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing/expected: Allergies, full medication reconciliation, vitals, physical exam findings, mood/depression screening.  
• Internal conflicts: Patient states can walk a mile without SOB but later notes minimal walking recently – conflict noted.  
• Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor overlapping/inaudible phrases, no impact on clinical content.
